definition: A general increase in prices over time, meaning each rupee buys a little less than before.
The interest rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks; it influences the interest rates banks charge on loans across the economy.
The total value of all goods and services produced within a country over a given period, used as the broadest measure of economic activity.
The gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue, excluding money raised through borrowing.
The gap that arises when a country spends more foreign currency (on imports, etc.) than it earns (from exports, etc.) over a period.
The situation where a country's imports (goods bought from abroad) are worth more than its exports (goods sold abroad) in a given period.
A single indirect tax applied to the sale of most goods and services in India, replacing several older separate taxes.
India's summer cropping season, roughly June to October, when crops like rice, cotton, and pulses are sown at the start of the monsoon and harvested in autumn.
A digital payments system that allows instant money transfers directly between bank accounts using a mobile phone, without sharing bank account details.
The percentage of people in the labour force (working or actively looking for work) who do not currently have a job.
